items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: And in Leo Williams's place on tenor saxophone we got a fellow who lived in Newark, New Jersey, and his name was Ike Quebec, which we became very good friends later.

ctx.x: Anyway, he did the engagement with us in Chicago, and after Chicago we went to New York in the Yacht Club, and I think Leo was with us for a short while. But for some reason, Leo left the band, and the alto saxophone player, Harry Curtis, got drafted into the Navy. So we got another kid who had grown up in Washington but was living in Baltimore at that particular time, and his name was William Swindell. We got him to play alto saxophone in Harry Curtis's place. And in Leo Williams's place on tenor saxophone we got a fellow who lived in Newark, New Jersey, and his name was Ike Quebec, which we became very good friends later. Ike was an excellent tenor saxophone player, plus he also played the piano. So that gave us a bond right there. I was trying to write then, and he would give me different suggestions about different things. For a guy his age... Because Ike was around
